1.consolidated_definition: Expresión que significa repetición de una acción. Copia las muchas construcciones que el inglés forma con back, to bring back, to call back, to come back, etc. , que españolizadas se construyen como: gritar para atrás, traer para atrás, volver para atrás, virar para atrás, llamar para atrás, etc. que pueden sustituirse por volver a llamar, llamar de nuevo, regresar, retroceder, etc. Neologismo anglicado, usual. Ella le insiste al padre que llega de la calle tropezando, que le grita, a quien ella le grita para atrás, que la persigue para darle y la agarra por el cuello, que hace llorar a la mamá, que se agarra la nariz por si acaso se suelta un puño —¿De quién?—
1.en_consolidated_definition:
Reiteration of an action; repetition of a deed. This expression corresponds to the English constructions formed with back, to bring back, to call back, to come back, etc., which, when Spanishized, are constructed as: shout back, bring back, return back, turn back, call back, etc., and can be replaced by calling again, calling anew, returning, retreating, etc. This anglicized neologism is commonly used.

Example sentence:
She insists that the father, who arrives from the street stumbling, shouting at her, whom she shouts back at, who chases after her to give her a hug and grabs her by the neck, making the mother cry, who holds her nose in case she lets go of a fist —Whose?—
